questions.stem: Prove that (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ = cosh nx + sinh nx for any n ∈ R.
If sinh x = 3, show that x = logₑ(3 + √10).
If sinh x = 5, show that x = logₑ(5 + √26).
If cosh x = 3, show that x = logₑ(3 + √8).
For any x ∈ R, prove that cosh⁴x − sinh⁴x = cosh 2x.
For x, y ∈ R, prove that sinh(x + y) = sinh x cosh y + cosh x sinh y.
questions.notes: Split from part ii): the two addition formulas are separate identities, each a whole question.

questions.stem: For x, y ∈ R, prove that cosh(x + y) = cosh x cosh y + sinh x sinh y.
For any x ∈ R, prove that sinh⁻¹x = logₑ(x + √(x² + 1)).
questions.notes: The book prints this as 'Theorem', not as a numbered exercise stem; it is still asked and worked like one.
